description: File name cleaning vectors. Spec: docs/protocol.md, "File names". For every case: cleanFileName(input, existing) must equal expected. existing is the list of names already in the destination folder. Strings use \u escapes for every non-ASCII character, so the file survives any editor. Lengths are counted in UTF-8 BYTES (the 200 and 16 limits); cuts fall on code point boundaries. createNew[] cases have an operation: create (the file is created for the first time; absent means create) or move_part (name.ext.part is moved to its final name): both use create-new semantics, 'already exists' takes the next suffix and is never a failure, any other failure is internal. For move_part, existing does not hold the transfer's own claim on the name.

cases.name: non-control-nbsp-kept
cases.note: U+00A0 and U+2028 are not control characters (category Cc)

cases.name: path-trailing-slash
cases.note: nothing follows the last separator, so the name is empty and becomes file

cases.name: path-slash-then-forbidden
cases.note: the path is stripped first, so a is gone before : is replaced

cases.name: control-at-end-not-stripped
cases.note: control characters become _ and are not trailing dots or spaces

cases.name: reserved-trailing-dot-stripped-first
cases.note: trailing dot is stripped (step 3) before the reserved check (step 5)

cases.name: reserved-space-before-extension
cases.note: trailing spaces of the part before the first dot are ignored for the check

cases.name: reserved-lookalike-leading-dot
cases.note: the part before the first dot is empty

cases.name: reserved-lookalike-after-replacement
cases.note: : becomes _ first, so the name is con_ which is not reserved

cases.name: reserved-before-length-limit
cases.note: prefix is added before the 200 limit; extension would be 251 chars, so there is none

cases.name: limit-ext-16-chars-kept
cases.note: extension including the dot is exactly 16 characters, so it is kept

cases.name: limit-ext-17-chars-dropped
cases.note: extension including the dot is 17 characters, so it is not an extension and the whole name is cut

cases.name: limit-multi-dot-only-last-ext-kept
cases.note: the extension is only the last .gz; .tar belongs to the stem and is cut away with it

cases.name: limit-cut-leaves-trailing-dot
cases.note: cut at 200 leaves a trailing dot, which is stripped again

cases.name: leading-dot-is-not-extension-long
cases.note: the only dot is the first character, so there is no extension

cases.name: leading-dot-collision-suffix-at-end
cases.note: no extension, so the suffix goes at the end

cases.name: double-leading-dot-has-extension
cases.note: the last dot is at index 1, so .bashrc is the extension and the stem is a single dot

cases.name: collision-case-insensitive-non-ascii
cases.note: case-insensitive by Unicode default lowercase mapping

cases.name: collision-ext-17-chars-suffix-at-end
cases.note: extension .0123456789abcdefg is 17 characters, so there is no extension

cases.name: collision-limit-with-ext
cases.note: the suffix must fit inside 200 characters, so the stem is cut by 4

cases.name: collision-limit-too-long-input
cases.note: input is cut to 200 first, that name exists, so (1) is added inside the limit

cases.name: limit-stem-cut-ends-in-space-with-ext
cases.note: the stem is cut to 196 characters (a x195 + space); trailing spaces of the cut stem are removed, so the name does not end in a space before the extension

cases.name: limit-cut-all-spaces-gives-file
cases.note: cut to 200 spaces, stripped to empty, so the stem becomes file

cases.name: limit-cut-leaves-reserved-name
cases.note: cut to CON + 197 spaces, stripped to CON, which is reserved

cases.name: limit-cut-leaves-reserved-name-with-ext
cases.note: stem is cut to CON + 193 spaces, stripped to CON, reserved: the name would have been CON.txt, a device name

cases.name: limit-cut-stem-all-dots-with-ext
cases.note: stem cut to 196 dots, stripped to empty, becomes file

cases.name: limit-cut-empty-stem-then-suffix
cases.note: the rule runs for every candidate: file is taken, so file + (1)

cases.name: limit-cut-reserved-stem-then-suffix
cases.note: the reserved-name rule runs for every candidate after a cut

cases.name: limit-uncut-stem-keeps-space-before-ext
cases.note: nothing was cut, so nothing is stripped

cases.name: limit-exactly-200-with-space-before-ext-not-cut
cases.note: 200 bytes: no cut, so the space before the extension stays

cases.name: limit-bytes-2byte-100-kept

createNew.name: create-new-lost-race-takes-next-suffix
createNew.note: a file appeared after existing was listed: the create call says already exists, which is a collision

createNew.name: create-new-case-folding-by-the-filesystem
createNew.note: NTFS treats the two names as equal even if the app did not

createNew.name: create-new-other-failure-is-internal
createNew.note: any create failure that is not already exists fails the file with internal

createNew.name: create-new-other-failure-after-a-collision
createNew.note: the retry after the collision hits a different failure: internal. createFails applies to every create that is not a collision

createNew.name: move-part-target-appeared
createNew.note: the transfer's own name.ext.part claimed photo.jpg, but a file with the final name appeared before the move. The move takes the next suffix and the stored final name becomes photo (1).jpg. existing does not hold this transfer's own claim. Never a 500

createNew.name: move-part-case-folding-by-the-filesystem
createNew.note: NTFS treats the two names as equal. A rename that replaces (Rust std::fs::rename) would have overwritten PHOTO.JPG

createNew.name: move-part-other-failure-is-internal
createNew.note: any failure of the move that is not already exists fails the file with internal
